service.name: flux-exchange
service.summary: Holds credentials, terminates channels, runs operations for many callers and records what happened. Its primary caller is an agent, not a human: people sign in to wire things up, and agents are what call operations all day.

capabilities.title: Read what this build could run
capabilities.summary: Every connector this deployment carries and every operation each one declares — what it is, what it costs, and what effects it has.

call.caller: Anyone. This route resolves no principal and takes no token.
call.note: One connector per entry, with the count of operations it declares; the operations themselves are at the same path under the connector id, at /api/catalogue/connectors/{id}/operations. It answers what exists, not what you may call — with no principal resolved every operation comes back admitted: null, which is a third value and not a refusal.

capabilities.title: Be issued an identity
capabilities.summary: An agent is a principal of exactly one tenant. It does not sign in: a human who already is mints it and hands over the token.

call.caller: A signed-in human, from this console. Not the agent — the route requires a principal, and an agent has none until this call has been made for it.
call.note: Send id, what to call the agent within the tenant, and expires_at, seconds since the Unix epoch. The expiry is never defaulted: a body without one is refused rather than given a lifetime this host picked. There is no tenant field, and there is nowhere one could be put — the tenant is read from the caller this host resolved, and a tenant in the body is ignored rather than honoured.
call.warn: The response carries the token, and it is shown once. This host keeps a verifier rather than the token, so nothing here can show it to you again. Lose it and mint another.

capabilities.title: Authenticate as that identity
capabilities.summary: Present the token on a request and have this host resolve you to the agent principal it minted, in that agent’s tenant.
capabilities.withheld: No route on this host accepts an agent token. Minting stores a verifier and hands you the token, and nothing yet resolves one back to a principal — so an agent holding a token is not a caller this service can identify. The only principals a deployment resolves today are humans who signed in through its identity provider.

capabilities.title: Call an operation
capabilities.summary: Name an operation and get a result, without naming a host, a credential or a tenant. The credential never crosses the boundary; the authority does.

call.caller: Any principal this host resolved. Today that means a signed-in human: nothing here yet resolves an agent token, which is the “Authenticate as that identity” step above — so an agent cannot reach this route until that one lands, however live the route is.
call.note: {operation} is the catalogue’s own id, as served at /api/catalogue/connectors, and the body is that operation’s declared parameters verbatim — there is no envelope, no tenant, no connector, no host and no credential, because every one of those is derived from the operation and from the principal this host resolved. The answer carries sent and retryable as fields, because an HTTP status answers neither: a 502 does not say whether the vendor received it. A vendor’s own 4xx comes back as 200 with its response in content, unshaped — the vendor said no and we could not ask are different events. A host with no credential store bound runs nothing and says so.
call.warn: This route is gated by identity alone. There is no grant model in this build, so any principal this host resolves may run any operation in the catalogue against its own tenant’s connections.

capabilities.title: Receive a vendor’s events
capabilities.summary: Have this host terminate a vendor’s channel, verify what arrives against the connector’s declaration, and hand you a typed event.
capabilities.withheld: `subscribe`, the websocket and channels are not built. Nothing here terminates a channel, so there is no subscription to show and no route to call.

capabilities.title: Read back what you did
capabilities.summary: Who asked, which grant admitted it, what was called and what came back.
capabilities.withheld: This service records nothing yet. There is no execution record to read, so there is no Activity screen — an empty one would say that nothing has happened, which is a different claim entirely.
